cases.name: plain-ascii
cases.covers: The dominant query.
cases.haystack: The cat sat on the mat.

cases.name: case-insensitive-by-default
cases.covers: A query with no flags ignores case, which is what a search box does.

cases.name: case-sensitive
cases.covers: matchCase keeps the fold from lowering either side.
cases.haystack: The CAT sat on the cat.

cases.name: accents-ignored-by-default
cases.covers: café is found by cafe, which is the fold doing its job.

cases.name: accents-respected
cases.covers: matchDiacritics keeps the marks, so cafe must not match café by stopping before the accent.
cases.haystack: Un café noir et un cafe clair.

cases.name: ligature-in-the-page
cases.covers: NFKD splits the ligature, so a two-letter needle finds a one-character page.

cases.name: ligature-in-the-needle
cases.covers: The same fold applies to what was typed.

cases.name: line-wrapped-phrase
cases.covers: A whitespace run collapses, so a wrapped phrase is still one match.

cases.name: needle-with-its-own-whitespace-run
cases.covers: Both sides collapse, so the query need not guess the page layout.

cases.name: whole-word-rejects-a-prefix
cases.covers: Concatenate contains cat and is not the word cat.

cases.name: whole-word-across-an-accent
cases.covers: The word test uses Unicode letters, so caf never whole-word matches inside café even after the accent is folded away.

cases.name: whole-word-against-a-non-ascii-letter
cases.covers: The word test is Unicode letters, not the ASCII set. A CJK character beside the needle is a word character, so this must NOT match; an ASCII-only rule would return a hit.
cases.haystack: 猫cat猫 and a lone cat

cases.name: whole-word-against-cyrillic
cases.covers: The same rule in another script, so the case is not about CJK width.

cases.name: overlapping-candidates
cases.covers: Matches do not overlap: the scan resumes after the one it took.

cases.name: empty-needle
cases.covers: Nothing searchable, which would otherwise match every position.

cases.name: whitespace-only-needle
cases.covers: Folds to a single space, which would match every collapsed run.

cases.name: needle-longer-than-the-page
cases.covers: The scan must not run off the end.

cases.name: no-match
cases.covers: The empty answer.

cases.name: sharp-s-folds-to-ss
cases.covers: The case round trip, which a plain lowercase would miss.

cases.name: astral-haystack
cases.covers: A supplementary character is two code units, so a match after it has to translate through the map rather than by counting characters.

cases.name: match-at-the-very-start
cases.covers: Offset zero, where an off-by-one hides.

cases.name: match-at-the-very-end
cases.covers: The last unit, where the other off-by-one hides.
